svg.text: PicoQuorum Build 1: Pico 2 W + 2.0" ST7789 240x320 + EC11 knob + key jacks (3.5 mm and 2.5 mm TRRS), ATECC608 key
Pico 2 W seen from the top, USB up. Numbers are physical header pins. A dot joins wires; wires that cross without a dot do not touch.
All power is 3.3 V from pin 36. Nothing here goes to VBUS (40) or VSYS (39). The pin table in hardware/wiring/BUILD1.md is the same one.
3 lugs one side: A, C, B
C is the middle of the 3
J2 tip: KEY VCC <- GP6, pin 9
J2 ring 1: KEY RST -> GP26, pin 31 (Trust M key; an ATECC key leaves it open)
J2 ring 2: KEY ID -> GP27, pin 32 (ADC1; open on every Build 1 key, dashed = optional)
screen 3V3 -> 3V3 OUT, pin 36. 3.3 V, never VBUS / 5 V
23 GND: the Sign button's other leg
free: GP0, GP14, GP16, GP18, GP20, GP22
dashed ring on the board = reserved pin, leave it free
The key, Build 1: the ATECC608 STEMMA breakout on a cut STEMMA QT cable, soldered to two plugs
Map each cable wire to the breakout's VIN / GND / SDA / SCL pads with a meter first (hardware/wiring/SOLDERING.md, section 1).
P1 ring 2 jumpered to P1 sleeve:
that is how the console sees
P2 rings: nothing on an ATECC key.
Trust M key: ring 1 = its RST pad
optional: 100 nF across VIN-GND at the plug
1. Screen VCC is 3.3 V (pin 36). Not VBUS, not 5 V.
2. Key power (GP6) is OFF before a plug goes in or comes out.
Every plug tip wipes past every jack contact, sleeve included:
a live GP6 on J2's tip gets shorted to ground on the way in.
The firmware turns GP6 on only after DETECT has read low
for 200 ms, and off the moment it goes high.
3. Never plug the key into a phone, laptop or audio jack.
Those drive the tip and put mic bias on a ring.
4. No 18650 without a PROTECTED TP4056 (the DW01 kind).
Build 1 runs on USB; the cell is a later build.
5. Config lock and data lock on the ATECC are permanent.
Build 1 only reads the chip. ALLOW_LOCK stays False.
6. Meter SDA/SCL/VIN/GND at the plugs before the first plug-in.
